name: Act of March 3, 1873 restoring part of the Round Valley reservation to the public domain (17 Stat. 633)
nations: Round Valley Indian Tribes (Covelo Indian Community)
promises: Not a treaty. The Act set new boundaries for the Round Valley reservation: the township line between townships 22 and 23 north became its southern boundary, with the Middle Fork of the Eel River on the east and the Eel River on the west.

The land south of that line, about 12,000 acres of the valley's agricultural land according to the Ninth Circuit, was restored to the public domain to be sold, and about 89,000 acres of mostly mountain land were added on the north.
Non-Indians living inside the new boundaries were to leave once paid for their improvements out of the proceeds of selling the former reservation land.
today: In Russ v. Wilkins, 624 F.2d 914 (9th Cir. 1980), the court recorded that the removal of non-Indians promised by the 1873 Act was never carried out because land sales did not raise enough money and Congress did not appropriate enough, and held that the Act of 1890 reduced the 1873 reservation. That ruling went against the Covelo Indian Community. The court also recorded a Secretary of the Interior restoration order of February 11, 1947 returning vacant land in the relinquished parts to tribal ownership.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 862-863
Russ v. Wilkins, 624 F.2d 914 (9th Cir. 1980)
sources.publisher: Caselaw Access Project, Harvard Law School

openQuestions: The Ninth Circuit quotes the 1885 Senate (Dawes) committee report calling the reservation's administration a "folly" and finding efforts to expel settlers feeble. That report was not opened; read at first hand it may be a government admission that the 1873 Act's promise was not kept, which would support "broken".

No Indian Claims Commission or Court of Claims decision about the 1873 restoration was located; the Round Valley peoples were within the Indians of California claims (settled), which were not read for this tract.
